1.stem: [Academic Talk — Meteorology] What did the mast measurements show about how the fog typically develops?

options.A: It begins as a low cloud layer that gradually settles to the ground
options.B: It appears in patches over the irrigated fields and then merges
options.C: It gathers first at the valley floor and thickens upward
options.D: It drifts in already formed from the lake at the valley's mouth

2.stem: [Academic Talk — Meteorology] How does the professor assess the modeling group's claim that the valley's fog can be forecast six hours ahead?

options.A: The claim is too modest, since the model does better than its makers report
options.B: The forecasts succeed by drawing on instruments that few valleys have
options.C: The skill disappears for exactly the episodes that matter, the deep and long-lived ones
options.D: It holds up: the model was verified on a winter it had not been trained on

3.stem: [Academic Talk — Theater History] What is the professor's main point about the surviving plot summary of Corvin's lost play, The Iron Garland?

options.A: It was a working document, drawn up to run the performance from backstage
options.B: It is one spectator's account, written down from memory afterward
options.C: It was posted as an advertisement to draw an audience in
options.D: It was prepared for the censor's office to review before licensing

4.stem: [Academic Talk — Soil Science] Why does the professor mention the handwritten weather diary kept at the farm?

options.A: It notes a flood around which the sampling schedule was later arranged
options.B: It was kept by the founder, and it corrects dates in his published papers
options.C: It lets the team tell weather swings apart from the effects of the treatments
options.D: It records field operations that the official reports leave out

5.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Cartography] Why does the professor discuss the Ferrandin atlas?

options.A: Its maker names the Salvera chartmaker in a preface, the sole written link between the two
options.B: It shows the coast after a harbor silted up, which brackets the chart's date
options.C: It copies the chart's mistakes, which settles which of the two came first
options.D: It survives in a dated binding, the one firm date in the whole group

6.stem: [Academic Talk — Ornithology] How does the professor respond to Dr. Vasquez's conclusion that the wrens' winter flocking is a response to predators?

options.A: She has the causation backward: the flocks form first and then draw predators in
options.B: The flocking appears in records made before the predator reached the region
options.C: The flocking she measured was an artifact of counting at winter feeders
options.D: Her account holds at the coastal sites but runs the other way inland

7.stem: [Academic Talk — Numismatics] What does the professor suggest about why the Tarveny hoard contains no small denominations?

options.A: The finders pocketed the small change before the hoard was reported
options.B: The mint had recalled the small denominations in just those years
options.C: Small denominations rarely circulated that far inland, and few ever reached the site
options.D: The small coins were bronze, and the soil at the site corrodes bronze away

8.stem: [Academic Talk — Materials Science] What does the professor suggest is likely to be the coating's first large-scale use?

options.A: The cables of suspension bridges
options.B: The legs of transmission towers
options.C: Ship hulls below the waterline
options.D: The interiors of water pipelines

9.stem: [Academic Talk — Numismatics] How does the professor respond to Teodorescu's argument that the hoard represents a soldier's pay?

options.A: He counters that it was a merchant's working stock, noting how the pieces were sorted by weight
options.B: He argues it is two separate deposits mixed together, which Teodorescu's reading cannot absorb
options.C: He rejects it: the mix of worn and fresh coins fits a family's savings, not military pay
options.D: He accepts it, since the total matches a cavalryman's annual pay too closely for coincidence

10.stem: [Academic Talk — Medieval Literature] What is the professor's main point about the lament section of the Lay of Ansfrid?

options.A: It was supplied by a later continuator, not the original poet
options.B: It exaggerates the genre's conventions in order to mock them
options.C: It reworks a passage from a chronicle the poet evidently knew
options.D: It follows a school exercise pattern taught throughout the period

11.stem: [Academic Talk — Materials Science] What is the professor's view of the Marek group's report that the coating's healing ability fades after a few repair cycles?

options.A: He is convinced, since several labs have now observed the same fading
options.B: He thinks the fading is real but caused by moisture, not by the healing agent running out
options.C: He traces the finding to a fault in the Marek group's testing rig
options.D: He notes that the group's own later trials walked the claim back

12.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Cartography] What is the professor's main point about the chart's place-names appearing in two languages?

options.A: The second set of names went in later, after the coast passed to new rulers
options.B: They reflect the mixed speech of the port where the maker worked
options.C: The maker compiled them from sources in two languages without reconciling them
options.D: They preserve a coastal dialect that no other document records

13.stem: [Academic Talk — Soil Science] Where does the professor come down in the disagreement between Halvorsen and Iwu over whether the plots' findings apply to working farms?

options.A: With neither, since both generalize from the same two crops without saying so
options.B: With Halvorsen, since trials on commercial farms have reproduced the plots' rankings
options.C: With Halvorsen's conclusion but not his reasoning, crediting a sister site's trials instead
options.D: With Iwu, because the site's soils were unusual from the beginning

14.stem: [Academic Talk — Meteorology] Why does the professor single out the Corvale campaign's second winter?

options.A: It provided the clear-night cases the comparison depended on
options.B: The equipment was relocated that year, so its records are analyzed separately
options.C: A road project cut through the site partway through it, splitting the record
options.D: It was unusually foggy, and most of the published findings rest on it

15.stem: [Academic Talk — Numismatics] What did the die study show about the most common coin type in the hoard?

options.A: Most of the coins were struck from the same few dies
options.B: The coins spread across many dies with hardly any links between them
options.C: The die links form a chain that puts the coins in minting order
options.D: Many coins pair an official die on one face with a locally cut die on the other

16.stem: [Academic Talk — Theater History] Why does the professor read out an entry from the company's expense ledger?

options.A: It fixes the date of a first performance that is otherwise unrecorded
options.B: It records a repair that reveals how the stage machinery worked
options.C: It shows rent still being paid on a playhouse the company had supposedly left
options.D: It names a partner who appears in no other document of the company

17.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Cartography] What is the professor's position on Perrin's argument that the Salvera chart was made for display rather than for use at sea?

options.A: He rejects it, pointing to wear along the folds from being carried and consulted
options.B: He argues it was a workshop pattern, kept for copying new charts from
options.C: He thinks it began as a working chart and was dressed up for show when it changed hands
options.D: He accepts it, since the pigments used would not have survived handling at sea

18.stem: [Academic Talk — Ornithology] What did the recapture records show about the territories of the older males?

options.A: They shifted step by step toward the wetland edge
options.B: They stayed in place from one year to the next
options.C: They contracted a little with each season the birds returned
options.D: They were swapped among neighboring males between seasons

19.stem: [Academic Talk — Ornithology] Why does the professor mention the wren population on Charby Island?

options.A: A storm there removed most of its birds, creating an unplanned experiment
options.B: Its birds descend from a documented release, so their ancestry is known
options.C: It is where the species was first described, decades before the mainland work
options.D: Its birds were surveyed with the same methods, making them the comparison group

20.stem: [Academic Talk — Materials Science] According to the professor, where did the fatigue tests show cracks in the coating first appearing?

options.A: Inside air pockets left behind while the coating cured
options.B: At the boundary between the coating and the metal beneath it
options.C: At spots where the coating had been laid on thickest
options.D: Along scratches picked up in handling before installation

21.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Cartography] What did the ink analysis indicate about the coastline running along the chart's northern edge?

options.A: It was added at least a generation after the chart was made
options.B: It was drawn first, and the remainder of the chart was built around it
options.C: It was worked on twice, in two inks separated by some years
options.D: It was drawn with the same batch of ink as the rest of the chart

22.stem: [Academic Talk — Medieval Literature] Why does the professor spend time on Ilse Brandt's edition of the poem?

options.A: Her edition introduced the stanza numbering that current scholarship still cites
options.B: Her edition silently combined two manuscripts, and later readings inherit the mixture
options.C: Her dating of the poem is the assumption on which later arguments rest
options.D: Her translation is where most students first encounter the poem

23.stem: [Academic Talk — Numismatics] Why does the professor bring up the second hoard, found across the river?

options.A: It was found still in its container, preserving the context the first hoard lost
options.B: Its latest coin matches the first hoard's, suggesting the two were hidden at the same time
options.C: Its excavation was recorded layer by layer, which the first hoard's hurried recovery was not
options.D: It holds the types missing from the first hoard, pointing to different sources

24.stem: [Academic Talk — Meteorology] What does the professor imply about the campaign's next phase?

options.A: Aircraft will sample the layer from above, which the earlier phases lacked
options.B: Routine monitoring will be handed over to the national weather service
options.C: It will be repeated in a neighboring valley chosen for its different shape
options.D: It will turn to how the episodes dissipate rather than how they begin

25.stem: [Academic Talk — Ornithology] What does the professor suggest about why females appear less often in the study's records?

options.A: Females lose their leg tags more often than the males do
options.B: Most trapping happens in months when females are sitting on nests
options.C: The trap lines run along ridgetops that females rarely visit
options.D: Females cross into the neighboring reserve, where trapping is not allowed

26.stem: [Academic Talk — Theater History] What does the professor suggest happened to the company after it disappears from the records in 1621?

options.A: It was absorbed by a rival troupe and vanished into that company's accounts
options.B: It dissolved when the lease on the Signet expired without renewal
options.C: It shifted to touring towns whose records have not survived
options.D: It continued under a new patron's name after the old patron died

27.stem: [Academic Talk — Materials Science] Why does the professor bring up Darex, a coating developed in the 1990s?

options.A: To describe a product whose failure left buyers wary of repair claims
options.B: To identify the coating whose test procedures the new studies borrowed
options.C: To contrast a coating built to resist damage with one built to mend it
options.D: To credit the source of the polymer the new coating builds on

28.stem: [Academic Talk — Medieval Literature] What does the professor say about the glosses in the margins of the Stavenow codex?

options.A: They were entered by two different hands working decades apart
options.B: They were copied from the exemplar together with the text itself
options.C: They are an early owner's finding aid rather than commentary
options.D: They were added by a reader correcting the scribe's dialect forms

29.stem: [Academic Talk — Medieval Literature] What is the professor's position on the claim that the Lay of Ansfrid was composed for oral performance?

options.A: He takes the oral features to be a written imitation of performance style
options.B: He finds the rhyme patterns decisive: they are built for the ear rather than the page
options.C: He is persuaded, but by the poem's direct addresses to listeners, not by its sound
options.D: He thinks the poem was reworked for performance after it had already circulated in writing

30.stem: [Academic Talk — Soil Science] What does the professor suggest about the experiment's future?

options.A: The plots will be kept exactly as they are, since any change would break the record
options.B: Field operations will wind down while analysis of the archive continues
options.C: The treatments will be updated across the plots to reflect current practice
options.D: Part of the land will be turned over to a newly designed trial

31.stem: [Academic Talk — Soil Science] What does the professor say the team concluded about what the early sample jars from the Ansdell plots actually contain?

options.A: Topsoil and subsoil mixed together in proportions no one recorded
options.B: Soil blended from points scattered across a whole plot
options.C: Soil from a single marked spot, returned to year after year
options.D: Soil taken mostly near the plot edges, where neighboring plots run together

32.stem: [Academic Talk — Theater History] What does the professor say the lawsuit records revealed about the company's shares?

options.A: They were held in equal portions by the eight principal actors
options.B: They changed hands so often that ownership could not be settled
options.C: A founder's widow held the largest single block of them
options.D: Most of them had been mortgaged to the landlord
